TTE preregistration: the OSF form

Source: vignettes/tte-preregistration.Rmd
tte-preregistration.Rmd

When to register

Do the OSF Preregistration when the specification YAML is final and the shared skeletons exist. s0 built the plan, you generated the Excel specification from it, and no stage after s0 has run.

Every answer of the form then comes from two files. These are the specification YAML, spec_vNNN.yaml, and the Excel specification, spec_vNNN.xlsx. After s0 the Excel specification holds two sheets, “Study Specification” and “Target trial protocol”. The protocol sheet documents one ETT, the first of the grid unless protocol_ett_id names another. Once s1 has run, a “Sparse conditions” sheet follows the Study Specification sheet when the spec has a sparse_rule. This article maps each OSF section to a YAML key and to a section of the Study Specification sheet.

Produce the Excel specification

$excel_spec_summary() writes the Excel specification from the plan that s0 builds. Run tteplan_check_spec() on the YAML first. It reads the YAML and no data.

swereg::tteplan_check_spec("/path/to/spec/spec_v001.yaml")

study <- swereg::registrystudy_load("/path/to/meta")
plan <- swereg::tteplan_from_spec_and_registrystudy(
  study = study,
  candidate_dir_spec = "/path/to/spec",
  candidate_dir_tteplan = "/path/to/plans/my_study",
  candidate_dir_results = "/path/to/results",
  spec_version = "v001"
)
plan$excel_spec_summary()
plan$print_target_checklist()

s0 reads the specification YAML and the registry codes of the RegistryStudy. It also loads the first skeleton batch to validate the specification:

  • It checks that each named column exists. It reads the outcome columns by name only, and reads no outcome value.
  • It reads the values of the treatment, washout and categorical confounder columns, and the type of the observation column.
  • It takes the last week of the data as the administrative end.

A failed check stops s0 or gives a warning. A message can state a count of prevalent-user weeks, or a category value that the data hold and the specification lacks. You MAY pass global_max_isoyearweek to set the administrative end yourself, and s0 then skips this validation.

tteplan_excel_spec_summary() writes the Excel specification from the specification YAML and a code registry, without a plan. It reads no skeleton, so it runs before s0, and while the skeletons do not yet hold a new code. Pass the RegistryStudy, or its $summary_table(), as code_registry, and each variable that the registry generates shows its codes. The Admin censoring: row reads not built (spec only) unless you pass global_max_isoyearweek. Every other cell matches $excel_spec_summary() at s0 for the same spec, code registry, period_width and protocol_ett_id. Do not edit the workbook by hand: change the YAML and write the workbook again.

Register after s0 and before s1.

The OSF sections, field by field

The YAML column names a key of the specification. vignette("tte-spec-schema") lists every legal key. The Excel column names a section of the Study Specification sheet, and a row label where one applies. TARGET items come from $print_target_checklist() on the same plan.

OSF section YAML key Excel specification
Research questions or hypotheses study$description, outcomes[], enrollments[]$treatment$arms Outcomes; Enrollments, rows “Treatment:” and “Comparator:”
Foreknowledge of data or evidence n/a n/a. See “Foreknowledge”.
Study type Non-randomized study. Adjustment or control-based design: the treatment and censoring weights. n/a
Intention for causal interpretation The estimands of TARGET item 6f n/a
Blinding of experimental treatments No blinding is involved. n/a
Additional blinding during research or analysis n/a n/a. See “Foreknowledge”.
Study design target_trial, enrollments[], follow_up[] Study, row “Design:”; Follow-up; Enrollments; the Target trial protocol sheet. TARGET items 6a to 6h and 7.
Randomization Not applicable. The comparator draw is seeded sampling, with enrollments[]$treatment$implementation$seed. n/a
Data collection procedures inclusion_criteria, exclusion_criteria, enrollments[]$additional_inclusion, enrollments[]$additional_exclusion, enrollments[]$observed_var Inclusion criteria (global); Exclusion criteria (global); Enrollments, rows “Additional inclusion:” and “Additional exclusion:”
Sample size n/a n/a. See “Sample size”.
Sample size rationale enrollments[]$treatment$implementation$comparator_to_intervention_ratio Enrollments, row “Comparator-to-intervention ratio:”. See “Sample size”.
Starting and stopping rules inclusion_criteria$isoyears, follow_up[]$weeks, the global_max_isoyearweek argument of s0 Inclusion criteria (global), row “Isoyears:”; Follow-up; Study, row “Admin censoring:”
Manipulated variables None n/a
Measured variables enrollments[]$treatment, outcomes[], confounders[], the criteria, subgroups[] Enrollments; Outcomes; Confounders; the criteria sections. The sheet does not list subgroups[].
Indices confounders[] with implementation$computed: true, and their source_variable and window Confounders, rows “Variable:” and “Window:”
Statistical models Fixed by swereg vignette("tte-methods"), section 1. TARGET item 6h.
Transformations n/a See “Transformations”.
Inference criteria study$implementation$conf_level, default 0.95 vignette("tte-methods"), section 1.8.6
Data inclusion and exclusion The criteria of “Data collection procedures”, and sparse_rule Confounders, rows of “Rare-condition rule (sparse_rule)”. TARGET items 6a and 7. See “The sparse_rule”.
Missing data Fixed rules, and the impute_fn argument of s1 vignette("tte-methods"), section 1.8.7. TARGET item 11.
Other planned analyses subgroups[], the untruncated weights, and the intention-to-treat estimand beside the per-protocol one vignette("tte-methods"), sections 1.8.8 and 1.9
Context and additional information study$implementation$version Study, row “Version:”. See “Deviations after registration”.

Statistical models

Section 1 of vignette("tte-methods") states the estimators as swereg implements them. Copy it without change, so the protocol matches the code. Then state each value of its list “Values your protocol must state”.

Transformations

swereg does not transform a confounder. The treatment weight model and the censoring models hold each confounder as one main-effect term, with no interaction and no spline. A numeric column enters as one linear term. A logical column enters as one term for TRUE. A character or factor column enters through the default treatment coding of R, so its first level is the reference.

Derive any other coding in the skeleton, and register the derived column. Section 1.8.9 of vignette("tte-methods") states the time terms of the outcome and censoring models.

Inference criteria

The intervals of the rate ratio and of the risk difference use study$implementation$conf_level. Standard errors are clustered on the person. swereg applies no correction for multiple outcomes or multiple comparisons. State your own rule in the form.

The sparse_rule

A sparse_rule block in the specification is a pre-specified rule. Each candidate confounder held by fewer than min_n persons in the smallest arm of the driving comparisons becomes an exclusion criterion of every comparison. The other candidates stay confounders. Each candidate is the variable of a confounder with computed: true.

confounders:
  - name: "Prior ischaemic stroke"
    implementation:
      source_variable: osd_i63
      window: lifetime_before_baseline
      computed: true

sparse_rule:
  min_n: 100
  decided_by: ["01"]
  candidates: [rd_no_osd_i63_everbefore]

decided_by names the driving comparisons. The rule is decided from baseline counts in the eligible population, before the comparator draw and without follow-up outcomes. s1 makes that decision.

At registration, nobody knows which conditions the rule excludes. Register the threshold, the driving comparisons and the candidates. The Excel specification states the rule and the row “Decision:” reads “not decided yet (s1 has not run)”. TARGET item 6a gives the same rule as prose. Paste it into “Data inclusion and exclusion”.

Sample size

At registration there are no study counts. Base the rationale on external information, such as a published incidence, or an earlier extraction that you document as such.

The minimum detectable effect (MDE) columns of the $export_tables() workbook are not a preregistration input. swereg computes them after s3, from the study’s own events.

To plan from external numbers, apply the naive Poisson formula that the MDE columns use:

mde <- function(rate0, py0, py1, power = 0.8, conf_level = 0.95) {
  e0 <- rate0 * py0
  e1 <- rate0 * py1
  se <- sqrt(1 / e1 + 1 / e0)
  k <- qnorm(1 - (1 - conf_level) / 2) + qnorm(power)
  round(c(
    comparator_events = e0,
    intervention_events = e1,
    mde_protective = exp(-k * se),
    mde_harmful = exp(k * se)
  ), 2)
}

# External rate: 4 events per 1,000 person-years in the comparator arm.
# 3,000 intervention person-trials and 6,000 comparator person-trials,
# with a 5-year horizon.
mde(rate0 = 4 / 1000, py0 = 6000 * 5, py1 = 3000 * 5)
#>   comparator_events intervention_events      mde_protective         mde_harmful 
#>              120.00               60.00                0.64                1.56

The person-years in this example are the person-trials times the horizon. That is an upper bound, because loss, death and the end of data stop follow-up early. The formula ignores the weights, and the repeated contributions of one person to many trials. So it can differ from the detectable effect of the weighted estimator with person-clustered standard errors.

Foreknowledge

At registration the authors ran s0 only, and s0 reads no outcome value. State that under “Explanation of foreknowledge”.

After registration, s1 reads outcome data. A person enters a trial only if they reach time zero free of every outcome of the enrollment. So every s1 count from the attrition step “Event before time zero” onwards depends on outcome events before time zero. The s1 panel files, file_raw and file_imp, also hold the follow-up outcomes. Do not open those files before the analysis. If an author sees an outcome-dependent result before the analysis, record it in the deviations log.

Deviations after registration

After registration, a change to the specification is a new specification version, with a new Excel specification:

  1. Copy the registered spec_vNNN.yaml to the next version number.
  2. Make the change, and set study$implementation$version and date.
  3. Build the plan from s0, and write the new Excel specification with $excel_spec_summary().
  4. Write one log entry: the date, the change and the reason.

Each version writes to its own results directory, because plan$dir_results appends the version. s0 stops when study$implementation$version differs from its spec_version argument. Do not edit the registered version. Compare two versions with git diff --no-index on their YAML files. Report the log with the paper.
